The history is exact. `checkpoint()` returns a token naming the current state — the number of unions performed so far. `undo()` reverses the most recent union and returns `false` when there is none left. `rollback(token)` undoes unions until the state matches that checkpoint and returns how many it undid. After a rollback the structure must be indistinguishable from the moment the checkpoint was taken: the same partition, the same set sizes, and the same representative returned by `find` for every element. Because tokens count unions, they are naturally used newest-first: a token that has already been rolled past no longer names a reachable state. 1: /**
2:  * Disjoint sets over the elements `0 .. count - 1`, joined by size and undone
3:  * in reverse order.
4:  *
5:  * Every union is recorded, so `undo` and `rollback` restore exactly the state
6:  * that existed before it: the same roots, the same component sizes, and the
7:  * same answer from `find` for every element.
8:  */
9: export class DisjointSets {
10:   #parent;
11:   #size;
12:   /** @type {Array<{attached: number, root: number}>} */
13:   #log = [];
14:   #components;
15: 
16:   /**
17:    * @param {number} count How many elements the structure holds.
18:    * @throws {TypeError} When the count is not a non-negative safe integer.
19:    */
20:   constructor(count) {
21:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(count) || count < 0) throw new TypeError('count must be a non-negative integer');
22:     this.#parent = Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => index);
23:     this.#size = new Array(count).fill(1);
24:     this.#components = count;
25:   }
26: 
27:   /** @returns {number} How many elements the structure holds. */
28:   get count() {
29:     return this.#parent.length;
30:   }
31: 
32:   /** @returns {number} How many disjoint sets exist right now. */
33:   get components() {
34:     return this.#components;
35:   }
36: 
37:   /**
38:    * Validates an element index.
39:    * @param {unknown} element Candidate element.
40:    * @returns {number} The element itself.
41:    * @throws {RangeError} When the element is outside `0 .. count - 1`.
42:    */
43:   #check(element) {
44:     if (!Number.isSafeInteger(element) || element < 0 || element >= this.#parent.length) {
45:       throw new RangeError(`element out of range: ${String(element)}`);
46:     }
47:     return element;
48:   }
49: 
50:   /**
51:    * Finds the representative of an element's set.
52:    * @param {number} element Element to look up.
53:    * @returns {number} Root element of the set.
54:    * @throws {RangeError} When the element is outside the structure.
55:    */
56:   find(element) {
57:     let node = this.#check(element);
58:     while (this.#parent[node] !== node) node = this.#parent[node];
59:     return node;
60:   }
61: 
62:   /**
63:    * Reports whether two elements share a set.
64:    * @param {number} a First element.
65:    * @param {number} b Second element.
66:    * @returns {boolean} True when both share a representative.
67:    */
68:   connected(a, b) {
69:     return this.find(a) === this.find(b);
70:   }
71: 
72:   /**
73:    * Reports how many elements share an element's set.
74:    * @param {number} element Element to measure.
75:    * @returns {number} Size of the set.
76:    */
77:   sizeOf(element) {
78:     return this.#size[this.find(element)];
79:   }
80: 
81:   /**
82:    * Joins two sets, attaching the smaller under the larger and, on a tie, the
83:    * larger root index under the smaller.
84:    * @param {number} a First element.
85:    * @param {number} b Second element.
86:    * @returns {boolean} False when both elements already shared a set.
87:    */
88:   union(a, b) {
89:     const rootA = this.find(a);
90:     const rootB = this.find(b);
91:     if (rootA === rootB) return false;
92:     let root = rootA;
93:     let attached = rootB;
94:     if (this.#size[rootB] > this.#size[rootA] || (this.#size[rootB] === this.#size[rootA] && rootB < rootA)) {
95:       root = rootB;
96:       attached = rootA;
97:     }
98:     this.#parent[attached] = root;
99:     this.#size[root] += this.#size[attached];
100:     this.#log.push({ attached, root });
101:     this.#components -= 1;
102:     return true;
103:   }
104: 
105:   /**
106:    * Marks the current state so it can be restored later.
107:    * @returns {number} Token naming this state.
108:    */
109:   checkpoint() {
110:     return this.#log.length;
111:   }
112: 
113:   /**
114:    * Undoes the most recent union.
115:    * @returns {boolean} False when no union was left to undo.
116:    */
117:   undo() {
118:     const last = this.#log.pop();
119:     if (last === undefined) return false;
120:     this.#size[last.root] -= this.#size[last.attached];
121:     this.#parent[last.attached] = last.attached;
122:     this.#components += 1;
123:     return true;
124:   }
125: 
126:   /**
